en.name: Spelt flour
en.summary: Spelt flour is milled from the same ancient hulled wheat as spelt berries, usually wholemeal or only lightly sifted, so the germ and its oil come with it. That oil sets the limit rather than anything microbial: 3 months in the pantry and 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
en.pantry: Three months in a sealed opaque tub, cool and dark. Spelt's particular quirk is its gluten. It is certainly there — spelt is a wheat and is not safe for coeliacs — but it is fragile and dissolves more readily than modern bread wheat's, which is why a spelt dough goes slack if you work it hard. Storage feeds into that: flour that has picked up moisture in a warm cupboard absorbs less water than the recipe expects, leaving you with a wet, sticky dough and no idea why. Keep it dry and the recipe stays honest. On age, trust your nose — spelt smells sweet and faintly of hazelnut when fresh, thin and paint-like once the oil has turned.
en.fridge: There is no refrigerated figure to give for spelt flour. The fridge does slow the oil and is a reasonable halfway house for a bag you will bake through over a season, provided the container seals; wholemeal flour is equally happy to absorb moisture and the smell of last night's dinner. Whatever you do, do not decant it into the fridge with the lid loose, and do not open it while it is still cold.
en.freezer: Six months at −18 °C (0 °F), the default for anything larger than a season's supply. Press the air out, seal it twice, label it. Frozen continuously it remains safe well past that, and what runs down is flavour as the oil oxidises slowly even in the cold. Warm the flour itself before mixing, not just the container: cold spelt flour hydrates slowly and the dough comes together stiff, and a stiff dough tempts you into kneading it more, which is precisely what its fragile gluten will not take.
en.thawing: Bring the sealed container to room temperature before opening so no condensation lands in the flour, and let the flour itself warm before you mix a dough.
spoilage: A sharp, oily or paint-like smell — rancid germ oil.
A bitter aftertaste in a bake that used to work.
Clumping or a hard cake in the bag, which means moisture got in.
Webbing, larvae or small moths, in which case the bag goes out.
tips: Decant into an opaque airtight tub as soon as you open the bag.
Buy what you will bake through in a season.
Handle spelt dough gently — its gluten is more fragile than modern wheat's.
Freeze a new bag hard for a couple of days to kill weevil eggs.

faq.q: How long does spelt flour last?
faq.a: 3 months in an airtight container in the pantry, or 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Seal it airtight, label it, and let it come back to room temperature before opening.

faq.q: How do you tell if spelt flour has gone off?
faq.a: Smell it. A sharp, paint-like note means the germ oil has gone rancid, and the bread will taste bitter.

zh.name: 斯佩爾特小麥粉
zh.summary: 斯佩爾特小麥粉是用和全粒斯佩爾特同一種古老帶殼小麥磨的，通常是全麥或只輕輕過篩，所以胚芽和它的油脂都留在粉裡。決定期限的是那些油，而不是任何微生物：常溫 3 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 6 個月。
zh.pantry: 裝在不透光的密封罐裡，陰涼避光，3 個月。斯佩爾特特別的地方在它的麵筋。麵筋當然是有的——它就是小麥，麩質不耐症的人不能吃——但它比現代麵包小麥脆弱、也更容易溶掉，所以斯佩爾特麵團一旦攪過頭就會垮。保存會直接影響這件事：在溫暖櫥櫃裡吸了濕氣的粉，吸水量比食譜預期的少，你會得到一團又濕又黏的麵團，而且想不出原因。粉保持乾燥，食譜才會誠實。至於新不新鮮，靠鼻子就夠：新鮮的甜、帶點榛果味；油一變質，味道就變得單薄而像油漆。
zh.fridge: 斯佩爾特小麥粉沒有對應的冷藏天數可以給。冷藏確實能拖慢油脂，對一季內會烤完的份量算是折衷方案，前提是容器密封得住；全麥粉對濕氣和昨晚那鍋菜的味道一樣來者不拒。無論如何，不要倒進冰箱後蓋子隨便蓋著，也不要在它還冰的時候打開。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 6 個月，超過一季用量的預設做法。擠掉空氣、封兩層、貼標籤。只要全程冷凍，安全性遠不只六個月，先用完的是風味，因為油脂在低溫下依然慢慢氧化。之後要回溫的不只是容器，粉本身也要回溫再攪：冰冷的斯佩爾特粉吸水慢，麵團會偏硬，而偏硬的麵團會誘使你多揉幾下——那正是它脆弱的麵筋承受不起的。
zh.thawing: 整罐密封著回到室溫再開蓋，粉才不會吸到凝結的水氣；調麵團之前也讓粉先回溫。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、帶油味或油漆味——胚芽油耗了。
一向沒問題的配方卻出現苦的餘韻。
袋子裡結塊或結成硬餅，表示受潮。
出現絲網、幼蟲或小蛾，整袋丟掉。
tips: 拆封後立刻倒進不透光的密封罐。
買一季內烤得完的份量。
斯佩爾特麵團要輕手操作——它的麵筋比現代小麥脆弱。
新買的整袋先冷凍凍硬兩三天，把蟲卵殺掉。

faq.q: 斯佩爾特小麥粉可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封放常溫 3 個月，或 −18 °C 冷凍 6 個月。

faq.q: 斯佩爾特小麥粉可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，−18 °C 下 6 個月。密封、貼標籤，開蓋前先讓它回到室溫。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷斯佩爾特小麥粉壞了？
faq.a: 聞一下。刺鼻、像油漆的味道就是胚芽油耗了，烤出來的麵包會發苦。
